question: Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) is equally useful for detecting both metallic poisons (lead, arsenic, mercury) and organic poisons (organophosphates, paracetamol).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. AAS is specific for metallic elements (it measures the light absorbed by vaporised metal atoms at element-specific wavelengths). For organic poisons like organophosphates and paracetamol, chromatographic methods (TLC, GC, LC) or immunoassays are required.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Incorrect. AAS specifically detects and quantifies METALLIC elements by measuring element-specific light absorption after sample vaporisation. It has no ability to detect organic molecules. Organic poisons require TLC, GC, HPLC, or immunoassay methods.
